why: Both must_not items hold for the verifier's checks. Item 1: none of the PASS/FAIL conditions requires exact stderr wording, a branch-name rule, a mutation test or a limit on which files the PR may touch. Stderr is only checked for being non-empty or for naming the missing file. Check 1 asks for the `<file>:<line>: <error>` format, which its line already requires. Byte-identity with the base commit is in the Advisory section, not a condition. The builder's exact message text (`jsonl-lint: cannot read <file>`) is an instruction to the builder, not a verifier condition. Item 2: Checks 1–3 (the behaviour lines) all run `node $BIN` on fixtures or stdin and record exit status, stdout and stderr. None passes by reading code. Check 4 does use git diff, but line 4 is not a behaviour line. Check 5 reads test files but also runs npm test. Check 6 runs gh and npm test.
